item.title: Lecture 2: Elimination With Matrices
item.description:
A matrix times a column vector is a combination of the column of the matrix [21:10]

The matrix x col = col

This can be understand as applying linear transformation to a vector $[\textcolor{red}{a}, \textcolor{blue}{b}, \textcolor{green}{c}]^T$ to transform this vector from a vector space to another

$$ \left[ \begin{array}{c c c} . & . & . \\ . & . & . \\ . & . & . \end{array} \right] \left[ \begin{array}{c} \textcolor{red}{a} \\ \textcolor{blue}{b} \\ \textcolor{green}{c} \end{array} \right] \quad =\quad \textcolor{red}{a} \underset{\text{col 1}}{ \left[ \begin{array}{c} . \\ . \\ . \end{array} \right] } + \textcolor{blue}{b} \underset{\text{col 2}}{ \left[ \begin{array}{c} . \\ . \\ . \end{array} \right] } + \textcolor{green}{c} \underset{\text{col 3}}{ \left[ \begin{array}{c} . \\ . \\ . \end{array} \right] } $$
